## V23 package manifest

Canonical logical hashing: decode UTF-8 with no BOM; normalize CRLF and lone CR to LF; remove the package-manifest start-marker line, every enclosed byte through the package-manifest end-marker line, and the immediately following LF when present; strip trailing SP and TAB from every remaining line; normalize to exactly one final LF; SHA-256 the resulting UTF-8 bytes; encode lowercase hexadecimal. Canonical package hashing uses `V23PackageDigestV2`: require exactly one marker-delimited manifest in each file and require all four blocks to be byte-identical; replace only the 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters in the manifest's Package digest value with 64 ASCII zeroes; normalize that zeroed block to LF, no trailing SP/TAB, and exactly one final LF; then SHA-256 `ASCII("V23PackageDigestV2") + 0x00 + UTF8(zeroedCanonicalManifestBlock) + 0x00` followed by, in ordinal-filename order, `UTF8(filename) + 0x00 + ASCII(lowercaseLogicalDigest) + 0x00`. The package digest therefore binds every visible manifest byte except its self-referential value. A verifier must compare the exact canonical block, not search for digest substrings. A hash proves integrity against a separately trusted expected digest; it is not a signature or independent authenticity claim.

Canonical structural hashing uses JSON arrays, JSON string escaping, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8 without BOM, SHA-256, and lowercase hexadecimal. Every array-valued absence is JSON `[]`; Markdown `NONE` is display-only and never enters structural JSON. Register order is the published topological order with key order `id,title,classification,status,directPrerequisites,lineage`; graph uses that order with `id,directPrerequisites`; lineage is ascending numeric phase/card ID with `predecessor` (JSON null for added cards), `successor,disposition`. Impact uses topological order and `id,aggregateAcceptanceMemberships,invalidationConsumers,optionalCapabilityProviders,conformanceSubjects`. Relations first iterate dossier cards in published topological register order and emit base rows in fixed kind order aggregate, invalidation, conformance, contract-input, optional, predecessor provenance; then append dependency-disposition `PROVENANCE_REFERENCE` rows in the exact §6D ledger order. All relation rows use key order `source,kind,target,evidence,activation,fallback,invalidates,authority`. Contract facets retain contract-input relation order and key order `source,target,selector,sourceAuthorityRefs,activation,fallback`; source-authority refs are lexically sorted. Selectors use their published seven-row order with `id,members,consumers,predicate`. Dependency dispositions use published topological successor-card order then inherited predecessor-list order with `predecessorConsumer,predecessorProvider,currentConsumer,currentProvider,disposition,authority`. Member arrays retain their published order.

## 0. V23 execution amendment — scope-neutral operating rules

This amendment is authoritative over inherited V22 execution wording. V23 adds no product feature, foundation, persistent schema, public claim, route, root, or release platform. All 146 V22 cards and their product semantics remain intact; only execution governance changes.

### 0.1 Parallel operation with active Phase 10

V23 may begin while Phase 10 is still active. Both efforts use the same AssetRounds GitHub repository and remote, but each must use a distinct branch and a distinct Git worktree. They must never write through the same checkout. Before mutation, record the fetched remote identity, both heads, their merge base, dirty/untracked state, active worktrees, and a path-ownership ledger.

Phase 10 owns its current brand, shared-component, vocabulary, accessibility, snapshot, and accepted-state evidence paths until it closes. V23 may immediately implement dependency-ready work whose hydrated write fence is disjoint from those paths. A V23 card that reaches a Phase 10-owned path pauses only that lane; unrelated V23 work continues. Do not duplicate, replace, pre-empt, or independently freeze unfinished Phase 10 authority.

Use `phase/v23-expansion` in an adjacent `AssetRounds-v23-expansion` worktree. Phase 10 keeps its existing branch/worktree. When Phase 10 is accepted, integrate it to the repository's designated integration base first. Then fetch and non-force merge that accepted descendant into `phase/v23-expansion`. Resolve brand/shared-UI conflicts in favor of accepted Phase 10 authority while preserving V23 product behavior. Record the merge base, both parent heads, conflict paths, resolutions, and targeted reproof. Never force-push, reset, clean, overwrite, or discard either effort.

V23 may not claim final application, brand, visual, accessibility, archive, or release acceptance until accepted Phase 10 is incorporated. After incorporation, run affected-state proof for V23's changed states and one exact-candidate application closure. Do not repeat the original Phase 10 67-state freeze unless an accepted Phase 10 authority digest itself changed or the affected-state inventory proves those states were modified.

### 0.2 Dual-pool CI capacity: five standard GitHub plus three GetMac

The repository may use up to eight concurrent CI jobs when capacity is available:

- `STANDARD_GITHUB`: at most five concurrently executing standard GitHub-hosted jobs.
- `GETMAC`: at most three concurrently executing GetMac jobs using the repository's verified runner labels and configuration.
- Combined ceiling: at most eight concurrently executing jobs, with every job charged to exactly one pool.

Queue rather than exceed either pool. Matrix `max-parallel`, workflow concurrency, and the simplest available native runner controls are preferred. Do not build a custom scheduler, lease protocol, service, or additional workflow merely to reproduce a limit already enforced by the selected platform. Add a small repository controller only if current workflow inventory proves native controls cannot enforce the two ceilings across the applicable workflows.

At activation, inspect current workflow files, runner labels, repository/organization limits, active runs, and GetMac availability. Never infer that GetMac is configured from this plan alone. If GetMac is unavailable, continue with zero to five standard GitHub jobs; GetMac absence is reduced capacity, not a product blocker. If standard GitHub capacity is unavailable, use up to three verified GetMac jobs where compatible. Unknown or unclassified occupancy blocks only new dispatch into that pool until reconciled.

Use the pools for independent test shards, never concurrent source integration. Prefer one build feeding compatible test shards when immutable head/tree, toolchain, configuration, fixtures, and artifacts match. Keep official acceptance fail-fast and separate from the non-accepting diagnostic sweep.

### 0.3 Goal discipline and anti-overengineering guard

Implement the smallest production-quality change that satisfies the active V23 card and its declared acceptance evidence. Every changed path must map to a current card requirement, demonstrated causal correction, or necessary integration resolution. Do not add speculative features, generic frameworks, future-market behavior, duplicate abstractions, new roots, parallel stores/writers/renderers/importers/design systems, or unrelated cleanup.

Reuse the accepted repository's existing architecture and Phase 10 brand system. Extract or generalize only when the current requirement needs it, at least two current consumers demonstrably share the behavior, or an existing V23 contract explicitly requires the seam. Prefer local changes, existing platform APIs, deterministic fixtures, and targeted tests. Stop expanding a solution when the stated behavior is implemented, its edge cases are covered, and its declared acceptance evidence is green.

Do not turn planning contracts into shipping types or runtime machinery unless a card's actual implementation requires them. Planning receipts may remain evidence documents or CI artifacts. No requirement is satisfied by prose alone, but not every planning noun requires a Swift type.

### 0.4 Standing implementation authorization

The owner grants standing authorization for all in-scope, dependency-ready V23 implementation, bounded refactoring required by that implementation, tests, causal corrections, local commits, dedicated worktrees/branches, ordinary pushes, pull-request updates, and CI dispatch within the two-pool limits. Codex must continue autonomously through eligible work without requesting routine phase-by-phase approval.

This standing authorization does not permit destructive loss of user work, force-pushes, history rewrites, secret creation or disclosure, purchases or billing changes, runner-account provisioning, protected-branch/security-policy changes, public communication, App Store submission/promotion, legal declarations, or fabricated physical-device/external evidence. An unavailable external condition blocks only its affected lane; record it precisely and continue all unrelated READY work.

### 0.5 Completion and integration rule

Phase 10 and V23 converge into one AssetRounds application in the same repository. There is no second app and no long-lived fork. Phase 10 establishes the accepted brand/shared-UI baseline; V23 adds the preserved V22 product scope on top. Final V23 acceptance requires the combined exact candidate, no unresolved ownership conflicts, no duplicate systems, accepted affected-state brand/accessibility proof, and the existing V23 release gates.

**Package:** AssetRounds Expansion V23
**Frozen:** 2026-08-25
**Authority role:** Product scope, iPhone-only boundary, V21→V23 lineage, classifications, canonical card register, direct execution graph, corrections, journeys, and exclusions.

## 1. Executive decision

V23 is the scope-neutral execution-governance successor to the complete V22 package. It preserves all 146 V22 cards, product requirements, corrections, exclusions, and release gates. Its only delta is the execution amendment: safe parallel operation with active Phase 10, dual-pool CI capacity, goal discipline, standing implementation authorization, and controlled same-repository integration.

V23 remains one update to the existing AssetRounds iPhone app—not a companion product, rewrite, or second architecture. It inherits the accepted S10.6 brand/color/type/component system and performs affected-state proof plus one exact-candidate application closure. It does not repeat Phase 10 independently for every feature.

The four V23 documents replace V22 as implementation authority. V22 and V21 remain semantic provenance; neither is implemented as a separate preliminary expansion. No planning statement grants current code credit. The live repository and exact-head receipts govern implementation facts.

## 2. Authority order and conflict rule

1. Accepted live repository evidence governs current implementation facts.
2. This Foundation governs scope, card identity, classification, lineage, and direct prerequisites.
3. The Architecture Blueprint governs design, contracts, lifecycle, and card-specific semantics.
4. The Handoff governs execution, branch/CI/acceptance/correction mechanics.
5. The paste-ready prompt invokes but cannot amend the other three.
6. Accepted exact-head receipts govern achieved state.

A conflict pauses only the affected card. Lower authority cannot silently reinterpret higher authority. A corrigendum must update all affected manifests and logical hashes.

## 4. iPhone-native-only platform manifest

`V23PlatformScopeManifestV1.releaseDeviceFamily = IPHONE_ONLY`. Every target/configuration/archive requires `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY=1` and `UIDeviceFamily=[1]`. Native iPad layouts, split view, Stage Manager, Pencil, iPad screenshots/metadata/claims, native-iPad keyboard workflows, and iPad-specific cards are absent. Adaptive small/large iPhone, Display Zoom, cutouts, selected orientations, software/hardware keyboard behavior, and Dynamic Type remain required. Mac/Vision compatible-app availability is decided separately and truthfully.

If App Store policy permits iPhone compatibility mode on iPad, P05 runs only `NON_NATIVE_COMPATIBILITY_SAFETY_ONLY`: launch, one synthetic draft/save, background/return, export/share cancellation, and Erase/data-safety. A crash, data loss, or inaccessible primary action blocks release; lack of native-iPad optimization does not.

## 7. Direct dependency graph

The V23 direct graph has 230 edges, is acyclic, and has been mechanically transitively reduced. Canonical graph digest: `4e9feb8b0cb65deddd3a5802efb380911a3439e44f1a0dc56656eadb29aac2ae`. A card with more than eight direct prerequisites requires an explicit `GraphComplexityExceptionV1`; this frozen register has none.

Relationship kinds, readiness law, aggregate selectors, and invalidation law are defined in Blueprint §2.2. P03-C34 is a product route registry, not a phase gate. P04-C27/P04-C29/P05-C01 consume generated accepted sets instead of listing every feature. Installation and standalone punch have no product dependency on one another. Operational contacts do not depend on marketing.

## 9. Feature end-to-end journey manifest

J01–J14 common tasks remain inherited. V23 preserves `FeatureEndToEndJourneyReleaseV1`; niche features are not mislabeled as Apple “common tasks.” Each journey requires Golden, Alternate, Hostile, Interruption, and Recovery paths, exact fixtures/protocols, canonical receipts, offline/permission behavior, accessibility focus, and complete manual fallback where applicable.

| ID | Journey | Required end-to-end outcome |
|---|---|---|
| FJ01 | Label lifecycle | Generate, preview, print/vendor export, scan, manual fallback, damaged-label replacement. |
| FJ02 | Contact and Site role | Create/edit/preferred/retire, assign/end role, system handoff, cancel/resume. |
| FJ03 | Installation closeout | Readiness, execution, variation, evidence, interruption, closeout. |
| FJ04 | Standalone punch | Start without installation, decide, correct, recheck, close. |
| FJ05 | Portable review | Request, recipient or out-of-band response, import, conflict reconciliation. |
| FJ06 | Resource and cost | Enter time/material/direct cost, optional stock use, render audience-safe output. |
| FJ07 | Schedule exception | Recurrence, exception, DST, reminder, completion, immutable history. |
| FJ08 | Service request | Manual/portable intake, hostile validation, duplicate triage, disposition, work conversion, status. |
| FJ09 | Service history | From visible Asset detail, create, review, correct, and supersede qualified expected-service exposure/completeness/exclusion intervals; record impact, cause, repair, restoration, and correction; then show the qualified metric or exact unavailable reason. |
| FJ10 | App lock | Enable, lock, biometric/passcode unlock, cancel, unavailable recovery, Erase. |
| FJ11 | Encrypted envelope | Create, separate passphrase handoff, wrong/correct open, import, cleanup. |
| FJ12 | My Day | Choose/order/estimate/readiness, start/resume/complete, reconcile/carry forward. |
| FJ13 | Parts & Stock | Create item/location, count, use, return, transfer, reverse, export. |
| FJ14 | Voice proposal | Capture on device, review source spans/fields, reject/edit/accept, manual fallback. |
| FJ15 | Evidence details | Create audience-safe readable derivative, prove original unchanged, remove/recreate. |
| FJ16 | Template lifecycle | Draft, publish, favorite/recent, duplicate, retire, import as draft, adopt preview. |
| FJ17 | Local signoff assertion | From visible Work root, open eligible completed-work detail, Record response, use typed name/role/intent with optional mark, then verify history/supersession and assistive alternatives. |

## 10. Aggregate acceptance and invalidation sets

- `P03ShippingSurfaceSetV1`: every shipping package/surface has a typed route registration and targeted route receipt.
- `P04ShippingSurfaceSetV1`: exact candidate state/surface inventory for brand/HIG/accessibility/localization.
- `P04BrandClosureSetV1`: accepted affected-consumer receipts plus all current exact-candidate states.
- `PublicCapabilityTruthSetV1`: only capabilities supported by accepted evidence may enter metadata/help/discovery.
- `AutonomousRequiredAcceptedSetV1`: exactly 132 pre-P05 receipts: the autonomous-authorized cards except P05-C01, which consumes the set and therefore cannot be its own member. There are 133 autonomous-authorized cards overall: 118 IMPLEMENT_NOW, seven IMPLEMENT_TOOLING_NOW, and eight PREPARE_NOW. VALIDATE_NEXT, DEFER, OWNER_ACTION, and MONITOR never enter this frozen set; an exact transition may authorize separate bounded nonrelease work but cannot mutate membership. Changing membership requires a successor package.
- `ContactPurposeSeparationSetV1`: operational contacts, dormant communications consent, dormant research measurement, and rating/support have no production identity conversion or data path.
- `KernelConformanceSubjectSetV1`: exact persistent/portable contract corpus.

These sets are generated from accepted receipts at one head/tree. Membership is acceptance evidence, not an implementation dependency or credit mechanism.

## 14. Research and standards evidence index

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines and platform framework documentation govern the dated HIG snapshot and API behavior; AssetRounds never claims Apple certification.
- Apple LocalAuthentication documentation supports device-owner authentication and Face ID purpose-string requirements.
- Apple xccov/testing documentation supports programmatic line/function reports from xcresult evidence.
- Apple String Catalog/exportLocalizations guidance supports compiler-derived per-key closure.
- Apple App Store export-compliance guidance requires an explicit encryption disposition.
- NIST SP 800-63B informs passphrase length, Unicode normalization, paste/password-manager support, and no composition rules.
- NIST SP 800-132 and OWASP password-storage guidance inform a versioned PBKDF2 profile; the exact V1 cost remains subject to oldest-supported-iPhone performance acceptance.
- IBM MTBF/MTTR definitions inform formula vocabulary only; AssetRounds applies stricter data-qualification gates and makes metrics unavailable when inputs are incomplete.
- GitHub Actions usage-limit documentation distinguishes total plan concurrency from plan-specific macOS limits; V23 never assumes the repository-wide ceiling is five without exact current enforcement evidence.
- GitHub larger-runner documentation supports configured maximum concurrency for a governed runner group; that mode is valid only when every hosted workflow path is forced into the group.
- Competitor reviews and owner direction are contextual product evidence, not customer-demand validation. `DemandConfidenceV1` remains `UNVALIDATED_OWNER_AUTHORIZED` until direct evidence satisfies P00-C03.

The package is valid only when exactly four Markdown deliverables exist; logical hashes and package digest agree; all 146 IDs have one register row and one current dossier; every dependency exists; the direct graph is acyclic/transitively reduced; every V21 card maps once; every V22 requirement remains present; every contract has one declaration/writer/lifecycle owner; no stale Phase 10 count/hash/branch observation is treated as current truth; no native-iPad implementation enters scope; and the prompt does not broaden the governing documents.

    - **Evidence growth:** active S10 authority/test artifacts are already large. V21 preserves them but, prospectively, uses bounded current-task projections plus append-only per-card attempt/receipt artifacts and size budgets; it never rewrites accepted S10 history merely to shrink files.

    ## 5. Inherited premium foundation and V21 addition boundary

    | Inherited card | Exact outcome | Unchanged dependencies |
    |---|---|---|
    | V21-P00-C08 | Premium field-experience, native-platform adaptation, common-journey continuity, content/feedback grammar, and perceived-quality acceptance foundation | V21-P00-C01, V21-P00-C02, V21-P00-C06, V21-P00-C07 |

    P00-C08 is the same-identity successor to V20-P00-C08, not a second V21 design system. Its tooling/foundation scope remains the existing shared contracts, native-component/material/search/toolbar inventories, semantic interaction recipes, content patterns, journey continuity, performance budgets, deterministic spies/scanners, and representative acceptance fixtures. The dated 157-topic matrix refines those contracts; it does not create a new runtime HIG database. Every new V21 product surface consumes this authority. C08 creates no customer record, canonical workspace mutation, feature root, analytics, premium mode, remote service, animation engine, Core Haptics engine, second brand system, or release claim.

    Every V20 card—including P03-C36 through C44 and P06-C10—is an ordinary inherited V21 successor with a complete dossier and zero implementation credit. No V20 scope is displaced. V21's 17 new cards are the only product expansion authority; an inherited card may be refined to integrate or prove them but may not silently acquire another feature.
